about.title: Los Altos Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Los Altos Hills residents often travel to nearby Santa Clara County hospitals and clinics for surgery, imaging, or specialist care, and most of those visits go the way they should. But when a physician, surgeon, or hospital staff member deviates from the accepted standard of care, the results can be lasting — a missed diagnosis, a surgical complication, or a medication mix-up that changes daily life. Because Los Altos Hills is a small, close-knit community, many residents rely on the same regional medical centers, which means these cases require careful review of records from providers who may serve thousands of patients across the county. We review what happened, gather the details, and handle your case directly. Our team has experience with California medical malpractice claims and works on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Details Matter in These Cases

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California's MICRA rules generally give you one year from when you discovered the harm, but never more than three years from the injury itself. We can help track which clock applies to your situation before it runs out.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice. Missing this step can delay or complicate a claim, so early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically must confirm that care fell below the accepted standard — a bad outcome by itself isn't enough. Our team can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: I live in Los Altos Hills but was treated at a hospital outside the city — does that matter?
items.answer: Not usually. What matters is where the care was provided and which standards apply, not your home address. Our team can look at the details of your treatment location and timeline to figure out the right approach.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered — or reasonably should have discovered — the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There are exceptions, so it's worth getting a professional opinion sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves real risks, and an unfavorable result on its own doesn't prove negligence. A claim generally requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified expert review is almost always part of the process.
